text: The ceiling comes down, and Borro catches it, the way he once caught a bridge.
But his field form is nearly spent. Fifty seconds, then the slab wins.
The only way on is under him and his four-metre slab. Jaeha waves them through.
Dami ducks through, then Woo with Uncle Pyo on his back, then Ho on all fours.
Jaeha's knees buckle with Borro's. He's carrying seventy percent of that slab.
Then two more keystones crack, one ahead and one behind.
Jaeha reads the roof like a trap floor. The cracks all start at the keystones.
On his blood-spotted page, he hands out the keystones like shifts.
Nib bends to jump. Lyra makes it clear this is not in an archer's job description.
Jaeha's grim half-smile says tonight, nobody gets to be just an archer.
He throws them both into field form. Borro's clock is down to thirty-eight seconds.
Nib braces his back against one keystone. Lyra braces both palms against the other.
That's three summons to carry, one over his limit. His body pays the difference.
He doesn't hesitate. His body has always been the cheapest thing on any raid. Carry.
Three threads pour into him, and he drops to his knees. A hundred and eighty percent. His worst yet.
The edges of his sight go grey. Blood drips onto the steel between his hands.
Moon Ahin takes one look at him and raises her baton. Her husks can share the weight.
Twenty husks press up on the stone, the cracks stop, and his load drops to one hundred and forty.
The green in Borro's eyes flickers like a dying bulb. Three seconds.
Everyone is through but Jaeha, and Borro spends his last seconds telling him to go.
Borro shoves him through one-handed. The green leaves his eyes, and the slab drives him flat.
Rest form now: no stronger than an ordinary person, pinned flat under the slab.
Jaeha crawls back to him. Borro's shell will hold, he says. He's happy to wait to be fetched.
Jaeha grips one huge finger in both hands. He already left one giant behind tonight. Not another.
On the safe side, the four crew stop and look back.
Uncle Pyo straps his bad knee tight and grabs a steel strut. Kanghan treated them like sandbags. Sandbags can push.
And all four run back toward the slab.
Moon Ahin sends ten husks down to help, and hates his surprised look. Apparently his rule is contagious.
Struts under the edge, husks lifting, Nib and Lyra pushing too, and Ho counting it out.
The slab tips off Borro's shell and slides into the water.
Then everyone collapses in one panting heap round Borro.
Borro looks from face to face, and thanks them. Slowly, so they know he means it.
Uncle Pyo laughs and cries at once. A decade in the traps, and it's his first thank-you.
Ho asks his new hyung if this is normal. Jaeha starts his old line about less screaming, then gives up. This is normal.
Ho is horrified. Woo laughs for the first time all night.
Jaeha tries to stand, and his legs fold. Severe strain, and seven minutes to the rim.
Moon Ahin holds out her hand without looking at him. At the ladder, she walked past his. Debt paid.
His bloody glove takes her white one, and leaves a smear of red.
They climb again, Jaeha on Moon Ahin's arm, Borro limping with Uncle Pyo on his cracked shell.
She can see what carrying all three is doing to him. He just won't die of it tonight.
She gives him a sideways look. Of all the numbers her family ever hired, he's the strangest.
Behind them, the boots have gone quiet. Somehow that makes Lyra more nervous, not less.
Jaeha knows why. Nobody chases a rat up a pipe when Han Sora is waiting at the other end.
The tunnel splits: one branch dark and dry, one following the water toward a faint white light.
Nib likes the dry branch. Jaeha follows the water, the one thing down here that knows how to leave.
Up the wet branch they go. Six minutes thirty-one.
Dami touches the crack in Borro's shell and asks if it hurts. Borro's answer is about someone else.
Dami looks up at Jaeha, and finally understands where all his wounds come from.
A small carved giant with a trident watches them pass, faded by centuries of water.
Lyra trails her fingers over it and repeats the merchant's promise to the stone. She believes it.
The tunnel ends at the foot of a long, steep shaft, white light at the very top.
Uncle Pyo has cleaned the pump room up there. Ten years of Kanghan's dirty work, and finally it pays: it's the only way out.
And at the top, a row of black shields, edge to edge.
Han Sora sits on a pump housing, swinging one boot, with twelve troopers behind their shields.
Her compass points straight down at him, and she's in no hurry. She's sitting on the only exit.
Everyone looks up the long slope at the shields.
Jaeha stands on his own and opens the notebook again. He counts the odds like traps. They're terrible.
Six minutes until the rim seals.
Twelve carbines take aim down the shaft, and Sora stands up and raises her crossbow.
